name: save-buffer-clear-bridge-and-count
body: Two limits. (1) `save` still calls `self.buffer.clear()`, and that call is load-bearing beyond the retired `end` gate: the in-memory admission list is where the next admission reads an identity's first-admission durability from, so clearing it at the durability boundary makes a later `rm` of an identity saved in this run read `durable_before = true` and record its ledger entry — without the clear, a node created and saved in one run and then removed would leave its now-durable file behind. Drop the call only when phase 3 removes the field itself, not when `end` stops reading the list. (2) The save's stdout count (`Session saved: N change(s) in one commit`) is pinned by two e2e tests — `save_flushes_the_buffer_in_one_commit` and `save_on_a_clean_buffer_is_a_noop` — so a reworded count must update them with it.
